🛡 AEGIS TOWER

AI-POWERED SPACE SITUATIONAL AWARENESS — PROJECT REPORT

v3.2.0  |  Random Forest ML Pipeline  |  CelesTrak SOCRATES Real Data
■ Executive Summary

AEGIS TOWER is a real-time satellite conjunction monitoring and collision risk prediction system. It propagates Keplerian orbits over a 48-hour window and uses three independently trained RandomForest regressors — trained on 903 real CelesTrak SOCRATES records — to predict miss distance, relative velocity, and collision probability for every tracked object pair. A premium 4-column React + Three.js tactical console displays all predictions live.

Left: R² scores per model (higher = better fit). Right: Mean Absolute Error per model. Miss Distance and Relative Velocity models achieve ≥89% R².

Left: Scatter of actual vs predicted miss distances — points clustered along the green perfect-prediction diagonal indicate high accuracy. Right: Residual plot shows errors are small and randomly distributed (no systematic bias).
■ Figure 3 — Relative Velocity: Actual vs Predicted
Relative velocity model achieves R²=98.44% — the tightest fit across all three models, reflecting that velocity differences are highly predictable from orbital element differences.

Left: Distribution of collision probabilities across all training records (log scale reveals the heavy-tailed nature of orbital conjunction probabilities). Centre: Risk tier distribution pie chart. Right: Actual vs predicted probability scatter (log scale).
■ Risk Classification System
Risk TierP(Collision) ThresholdTraining Records% of DatasetAction Required
HIGH P(c) ≥ 1 × 10⁻³ 344 38.1% Critical warning popup + immediate maneuver review
MEDIUM 5 × 10⁻⁵ ≤ P(c) < 10⁻³ 379 42.0% Monitor closely, track probability trend
LOW P(c) < 5 × 10⁻⁵ 180 19.9% Continue nominal satellite operations
■ Figure 5 — Risk Tier Classification Accuracy
Overall risk tier classification accuracy: 19.3%. Left: Per-tier accuracy bars. Right: Total vs correctly classified sample counts per tier.
■ Figure 6 — Feature Importances
Feature importances for all three RandomForest models. Orbital element differences (inclination, RAAN, semi-major axis) dominate prediction performance. Debris flags provide additional signal for collision probability.
■ Input Features
#FeatureDescriptionOrbital Significance
1inc_diffInclination difference (°)Determines relative orbital plane crossing angle
2raan_diffRAAN difference (°)Right ascension of ascending nodes — plane orientation
3ecc_diffEccentricity differenceOrbit shape dissimilarity — affects approach geometry
4arg_perigee_diffArgument of perigee difference (°)Closest orbital point orientation
5mean_motion_diffMean motion difference (rev/day)Relative angular velocity in orbit
6a_diffSemi-major axis difference (km)Orbit size — determines altitude separation
7alt_diffAltitude difference (km)Direct measure of vertical separation
8is_debris1Primary object is debris (0/1)Debris objects have no active collision avoidance
9is_debris2Secondary object is debris (0/1)Debris objects have no active collision avoidance
